# Wait for boxd to list a machine `BoxdSandboxBackend` just created instead of reporting it missing

Closes #14118

### Why we make these changes

boxd's `machines.get` can answer "VM not found" for a moment after `machines.create` returns. `BoxdSandboxBackend._wait_until_ready` treated every `NotFoundError` as final, so a fresh backend's first operation could fail with "was not found (it was deleted, or never existed ...)" for the machine it had just created. The live nightly hit this twice: [2026-11-21](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/actions/runs/44865703531) and [2026-11-16](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/actions/runs/43804167384).

Now a backend that created a machine keeps looking it up for up to 90 s after creating it (`_UNLISTED_TIMEOUT`), until a lookup finds it. That holds across operations, so it also covers a creating call that was cancelled while it waited. Once a lookup has found the machine, not found means it's gone, and an attach by `ref` still raises `WorkspaceUnavailableError` at once.

### New public surface

None.

### User-visible behavior

### What changes for existing users

A fresh `BoxdSandbox` no longer fails its first operation on a machine boxd hasn't listed yet, and a new machine that never appears now fails after 90 s instead of at once, with the same `WorkspaceUnavailableError`.

# Deprecate `clai` in favour of pax (`pydantic-ai-pax`)

- Fixes #9356

Deprecates `clai` in favour of pax (`pydantic-ai-pax`), as #9356 and #13393 intend.

- `clai` and `python -m pydantic_ai` print a deprecation note to stderr, then run as before. The note says `clai` will be removed in v3, how to install pax, and links to the migration guide.
- `docs/cli.md` gets a deprecation banner and a "Migrating to pax" section that maps `clai` invocations to `pax` ones, including `clai web` and `--mcp-config`. It also notes that pax loads `coder` (file edits and shell) by default, unlike `clai`. `docs/web.md` and `clai/README.md` link to it.

Decisions on the open items in #9356 (the maintainer driving this asked to deprecate now, ahead of the "after pax goes beta" timing in #13393):

- **Timeline:** the note ships with the release that first publishes `pydantic-ai-pax`, and `clai` is removed in v3, following the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md).
- **Parity:** pax covers chat, one-shot prompts, `-m`, `-a module:variable` and MCP servers. It does not yet cover `clai web` (`pax --web` cannot serve an agent passed with `-a`; `Agent.to_web()` is the replacement), agent spec files for `-a`, `--no-stream`, `--list-models` or `--code-theme`. The docs list each gap, with a workaround where one exists. A maintainer should decide whether any of these gaps must close before the note ships.
- **Feature work:** new features go to pax. `clai` only gets fixes, and the docs banner says so.

Other choices:

- The note is a plain stderr line, not `warnings.warn`, so it matches the `clai2` shim in #13885. A warning would show the shim's file and line, which mean nothing to someone running a command. It is emitted from `cli_exit`, the entry point that `clai` and `python -m pydantic_ai` share. `Agent.to_cli()`, `to_cli_sync()` and `to_web()` stay undeprecated, and the docs say so.
- Several pages still show `uvx ... clai -a pydantic_ai_harness.<x>:<x>_agent` examples: the front pages, the Harness coder and researcher pages, and the twin READMEs of those pages. I left them unchanged, because `pydantic-ai-pax` isn't on PyPI until #13885 is released. Switching them to `uvx pydantic-ai-pax -a ...` is tracked in #13895, for after that release. `docs/interfaces.md` already marks `clai` as deprecated.

This changes core code outside `pydantic_ai_harness` (`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_cli`), so it needs Aditya's (@adtyavrdhn) review.

# Keep `include_baggage` in control of online evaluation event baggage on logfire 6

Closes #14071
Closes #14073

### Why we make these changes

logfire 6.0.0 copies the baggage of a log record's context onto the record when `add_baggage_to_attributes` is on, its default ([pydantic/logfire#2788]()). That bypasses the documented `include_baggage` contract for `gen_ai.evaluation.result` events: with `include_baggage=False` the events still carry baggage, and baggage can set `logfire.scorer.*` keys a record omits. The latest-versions canary caught both.

`emit_otel_events` now emits each record with the baggage cleared from its context. The parent span stays in that context, so events stay nested under the evaluated call. `include_baggage` and the reserved `logfire.scorer.*` filter are again the only way baggage reaches an event.

### Cap or migrate

[Pydanty's triage](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/14071#issuecomment-7034907219) weighed capping `logfire<6` against migrating with per-call baggage isolation, which it had not tested. This PR migrates:

- **Per-call isolation, tested.** Each event's record context carries no baggage, on logfire 5.6.0 and 6.0.0. The user's global logfire configuration is untouched.
- **Same output on both versions.** Exported events are identical on 5.6.0 and 6.0.0.
- **A cap would be worse.** It would block every `pydantic-evals` user from logfire 6, and still leave users who install logfire 6 explicitly with the broken contract.

### New public surface

None.

### User-visible behavior

With logfire 6 and `OnlineEvalConfig(include_baggage=False)`, a call made under baggage `tenant=acme`:

### What changes for existing users

On logfire 6, evaluation events match the documented `include_baggage` behavior again. On logfire 5, events are unchanged. A custom log processor that reads baggage from a record's context no longer finds any on evaluation events; it can read them from the event's attributes (with `include_baggage=True`) or from the current context instead.

# Check the OpenAI conversation before `openai_conversation_id` trims history through a response whose stream dropped

Closes #13264

### Why we make these changes

With `openai_conversation_id`, `OpenAIResponsesModel` records the conversation ID when a stream starts, and the next request sends only what came after that response. OpenAI adds a response to its conversation only once the response completes ([reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create)). So after a stream dropped, the continuation sent the synthesized `function_call_output` for a `function_call` the conversation never received, and OpenAI rejects that with 400 "No tool call found for function call output".

For a response that was cut off before it finished (`state='interrupted'`, no `finish_reason`), the adapter now looks its output items up in the conversation before trimming through it, as [OpenAI advises](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2571#issuecomment-5701611363).

### New public surface

None.

### User-visible behavior

Continuing after a stream dropped once `lookup` was called, when the conversation doesn't hold that response:

- before: `[function_call_output(call_1), user 'Continue']`, rejected with 400
- after: `[user 'Look up a value', function_call(call_1), function_call_output(call_1), user 'Continue']`

### What changes for existing users

Only a continuation through a response whose stream dropped or was cancelled, with `openai_conversation_id` set, changes: it makes one conversation-items request, and resends that turn when the conversation doesn't hold it.

<details>
<summary>Live probe against the OpenAI API (2026-11-19)</summary>

OpenAI SDK only, `gpt-4.1-mini` and `gpt-5-mini`, throwaway conversations.

- 9 of 9 streams the client dropped (after `response.created`, after a function call's `output_item.added`, after its `output_item.done`) left the conversation's items empty, immediately and 10 s later.
- `responses.retrieve` on those responses returned `completed` once and 404 eight times, so it is not a commit signal.
- Conversation item IDs equal the response's output item IDs (`fc_…`), which is what the lookup matches.
- Trimmed continuation on the uncommitted conversation: 400 "No tool call found for function call output with call_id …".
- Resending prompt, `function_call`, `function_call_output` and the new prompt: 200, for `gpt-4.1-mini` without item IDs and `gpt-5-mini` with and without them.
- On a conversation that did hold the turn: resending it without item IDs duplicated the items; with IDs it got 400 "Duplicate item found with id fc_…". That is why the adapter checks rather than always resending.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Deliberately out of scope</summary>

- `openai_previous_response_id` chaining through a dropped response: a dropped response returned 404 on retrieve in 8 of 9 probes, so it likely fails too, but it is not reproduced here.
- A stream that ends cleanly without `response.completed`: it is recorded `complete` with no `finish_reason`, so the gate above doesn't reach it. Tracked by #10382; how conversation reuse should treat such a response depends on the state decision there.
- `openai_send_reasoning_ids=True` on a non-reasoning model: in the probe, a resent `function_call` with its item ID was accepted but left out of the conversation. Not a default configuration.
- If OpenAI did hold the response and produced more output after the client's stream dropped, the continuation answers only the calls the client saw, as before this PR.

</details>

`THREAT_MODEL.md`: no trigger; the lookup goes to the endpoint and conversation the request already uses, and only item IDs are compared.

<details>
<summary>PR decisions</summary>

# Make the Codex sign-in URL a clickable OSC 8 hyperlink in `clai2`

- Closes #14004

The Codex sign-in URL is now a clickable OSC 8 terminal hyperlink. Browser opening still goes through `pydantic_clai2.ui.browser.open_browser`, which wraps the standard library `webbrowser` module. A regression test now pins that.

**Changes**

- `auth.py`: the terminal sign-in prints the authorization URL as a Rich `Text` with `Style(link=url)`. Rich wraps the long URL over several lines, and each line links to the whole URL. The transcript keeps that link metadata, so the link also survives into native scrollback. The browser is still opened with `open_browser(url)`.
- `ui/menus/dialogs.py`: `TerminalDialogs.wait` makes each URL in its preview an OSC 8 link with termflow's `make_link`. A URL whose line fits the preview pane shows unchanged. termflow cuts any line wider than the pane, and that cut would also drop a link's closing escape. So a line with a URL that is too long is folded at the pane's width, and each row links to the whole URL, as Rich does. The full URL stays visible and copyable even in terminals without OSC 8. Lines without a URL are left as they were. The screen reuses `prompt_selection`'s URL pattern (now public as `URL`) and `trim_url`, so trailing punctuation is left out of the link. It only links URLs of up to `MAX_LINK` (2048) characters, a constant now exported from `rendering.py` and shared with `LinkOutput`. Longer URLs, and URLs with non-printable characters, stay plain text.

none

|---|---|---|

The issue listed four options. I picked **option 1** (keep `kind='external'`/`'unapproved'` tools native under `'all'`, with explicit selectors still able to opt them in):

- It makes the default safe without a warning about tools that are exposed but can't work (option 3).
- Option 2 needs a run-scoped way to tell whether an inline handler will resolve a call. - Option 4 is the same policy expressed as a new selector value; scoping the exclusion to `'all'` gets it without a new public type.

- `CodeModeToolset._selects` applies the `'all'` exclusion via `ToolDefinition.defer`, used for placement, hidden-tool placement and discovery announcements.

# Restore empty `tool_args` when Anthropic streams a zero-argument `mcp_tool_use`

- Closes #10284

When `AnthropicModel` streamed an `mcp_tool_use` for an MCP tool with no arguments, the stored `NativeToolCallPart.args` ended in `"tool_args":}` (invalid JSON), so the next request dropped the `mcp_tool_use` but still sent its `mcp_tool_result`, and Anthropic rejected it with a 400. At `content_block_stop` the stream handler now restores the `{}` it dropped at block start when no input JSON arrived (no delta, or an empty one), so the args are `{"action":"call_tool","tool_name":"who_am_i","tool_args":{}}` and the pair replays.

Calls with arguments still get the same deltas and final args (`test_anthropic_mcp_servers_stream`), and non-streaming replay is untouched (`test_anthropic_mcp_call_replays_empty_tool_args`). Already-stored histories with `"tool_args":}` and dropping orphaned `mcp_tool_result` blocks are out of scope here and left for a maintainer decision.

Tests: `test_anthropic_mcp_call_streams_empty_tool_args` streams a zero-argument `mcp_tool_use` (with no input delta, and with an empty one) and asserts the stored args are valid JSON with `tool_args: {}`; both cases fail on `main`. Replay of those args is already pinned by `test_anthropic_mcp_call_replays_empty_tool_args`, so the new test doesn't replay.

Fixes invalid JSON in streamed Anthropic MCP tool calls with no arguments, which caused the next request to drop the tool use and be rejected with a 400.

When `AnthropicModel` streamed an `mcp_tool_use` for a tool with no arguments, the stored `NativeToolCallPart.args` ended in `"tool_args":}`. # Keep the stale-thinking-block recovery of `AnthropicModel.count_tokens` for later counts when the request carries a `ModelSettingsDeltaPart`

> This pull request was posted by Claude Code using claude-opus-5-5 on behalf of David.

No linked issue: a self-found defect.

### Why we make these changes

When Anthropic rejects a count for a stale thinking block, `AnthropicModel.count_tokens` retries with `drop_block` and marks the conversation's last `ModelRequest`, so later counts ask for the drop up front. When that request holds a `ModelSettingsDeltaPart` the count drops and has no `metadata` yet, `_effort_delta_request` hands back a copy of the request, and the mark landed on the copy. Every later count then hit the 400 again, retried, and warned again. The count now marks the caller's request.

A run with `thinking='high'` records that part on its request, so `UsageLimits(count_tokens_before_request=True)` on a model that binds thinking blocks hits this on every turn.
